places.name: Amman
places.summary: Jordan's hilly capital, with the Roman theatre, the Citadel and the busy souks of downtown (al-Balad) at its core. The natural arrival point and a good base for day trips to Jerash, the Dead Sea and the desert castles.
facts: Downtown is walkable; taxis are cheap for the hills (insist on the meter)
Try falafel and hummus downtown and knafeh at Habibah
Traffic is heavy at rush hour; start day trips early
Many shops close or open late on Friday
places.season: Pleasant in spring and autumn; winters are cool and it can even snow, summers hot but drier than the lowlands.

places.name: Amman Citadel (Jabal al-Qal'a)
places.summary: Hilltop ruins inhabited since the Bronze Age, with the Temple of Hercules, a Byzantine church and the Umayyad Palace. Gives the best views over downtown Amman and the Roman theatre.
facts: ~3 JOD; Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Includes the Jordan Archaeological Museum
Best light in late afternoon; short taxi ride from downtown
Allow 1–1.5 hours

places.name: Roman Theatre
places.summary: Restored 2nd-century theatre for about 6,000 spectators cut into the hillside below the Citadel. Small folklore and costume museums are built into its wings, and the Odeon and Hashemite Plaza are next to it.
facts: ~2 JOD; Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Climb to the top rows for the view
In downtown, walking distance from the souks

places.name: The Jordan Museum
places.summary: The national museum in Ras al-Ain, covering Jordan's history from prehistory to today. It holds the 'Ain Ghazal statues, some of the oldest large human figures known, and pieces of the Dead Sea Scrolls.
facts: ~5 JOD for foreigners
Closed on Tuesdays
Allow 1.5 hours; good on a hot afternoon

places.name: King Abdullah I Mosque
places.summary: Large modern mosque from 1989 with a blue mosaic dome, one of the few in Jordan that welcomes non-Muslim visitors inside. A small Islamic museum is attached.
facts: Small entry fee (~2 JOD) for non-Muslims
Modest dress required; women get an abaya at the entrance
Closed to visitors at Friday prayers

places.name: Grand Husseini Mosque
places.summary: Pink-and-white mosque at the heart of downtown, rebuilt in 1924 on the site of a 7th-century mosque. The streets around it are the busiest part of the souk.
facts: Usually viewed from outside; non-Muslims are not always admitted
Avoid prayer times, especially Friday midday
In the middle of the downtown souk

places.name: Rainbow Street (Jabal Amman)
places.summary: Lively street of cafes, rooftop bars and small shops in the old Jabal Amman district, with 1920s stone houses on the side lanes. Busy in the evening and on the Friday Souk Jara market in summer.
facts: Best in the evening
Souk Jara flea market on summer Fridays
Walk down the stairs to downtown

places.name: Darat al Funun
places.summary: Contemporary Arab art centre in restored 1920s villas on Jabal al-Weibdeh, with gardens built over the ruins of a Byzantine church. A quiet green escape above downtown.
facts: Free entry
Combine with the cafes of Jabal al-Weibdeh
Allow about 1 hour

places.name: Royal Automobile Museum
places.summary: Collection of the Hashemite royal family's cars and motorbikes in King Hussein Park, telling the story of modern Jordan through them. Good for car enthusiasts and families.
facts: Small entry fee
In King Hussein Park, west Amman; reach by taxi
Allow about 1 hour

places.name: Iraq al-Amir & Qasr al-Abd
places.summary: Rare Hellenistic palace of the 2nd century BC with carved lions and leopards, in a green valley west of Amman. Nearby cliffs have caves that gave the village its name, and a women's craft cooperative.
facts: Small entry fee; Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
About 35 minutes' drive from Amman
Pretty in spring when the valley is green

places.name: As-Salt
places.summary: Hill town of honey-coloured Ottoman merchant houses on steep stairways, a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2021. Calmer and more traditional than Amman, with a good historical museum in the Abu Jaber house.
facts: Walk Hammam Street souk and the stairways
Abu Jaber Museum and the Historic Old Salt Museum
35–40 minutes from Amman

places.name: Abu Darwish Mosque
places.summary: Striking black-and-white chequered mosque built in 1961 on Jabal al-Ashrafieh, one of Amman's highest hills. Worth a quick stop for the architecture and the city views.
facts: Usually viewed from outside
Short taxi ride from downtown
Best views of Amman from the surrounding hill

places.name: Jerash
places.summary: Modern market town built around one of the best-preserved Roman cities anywhere. Usually a day trip from Amman, but a few guesthouses let you see the ruins early and combine with Ajloun.
facts: Under an hour from Amman
Lebanese House restaurant is a classic lunch stop
Combine with Ajloun Castle the same day

places.name: Ancient Jerash (Gerasa)
places.summary: Vast Greco-Roman city with Hadrian's Arch, the oval forum, a colonnaded street, two theatres and the Temple of Artemis. One of the best-preserved Roman provincial towns in the world.
facts: ~10 JOD; Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Allow 3 hours; bring water and a hat, there is little shade
Roman army and chariot show (RACE) runs some days for an extra fee
Arrive at opening to beat tour buses
places.season: Very hot at midday in summer; spring brings wildflowers among the columns.

places.name: Ajloun
places.summary: Hill town in the green north, below its Ayyubid castle and close to the Ajloun Forest Reserve. A good base for hiking and village homestays.
facts: Guesthouses and RSCN cabins nearby
Cooler than Amman in summer
Base for the castle, the forest reserve and village homestays

places.name: Ajloun Castle (Qal'at ar-Rabad)
places.summary: 12th-century Ayyubid castle built by a general of Saladin to watch the Jordan Valley and the iron mines. Well-preserved halls and towers and wide views to the West Bank on clear days.
facts: ~3 JOD; Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Small museum inside
Allow 1 hour; parking at the gate

places.name: Ajloun Forest Reserve
places.summary: RSCN reserve of evergreen oak, pistachio and strawberry-tree woodland, with marked trails and the Soap House and Biscuit House village projects. A green contrast to the rest of Jordan.
facts: Some trails need an RSCN guide; book at the lodge
Cabins and tents for overnight stays
Best in spring (March–May)
places.season: Spring is lush and full of flowers; winter can be wet and cold.

places.name: Umm Qais (Gadara)
places.summary: Black-basalt Roman city of the Decapolis on a ridge in the far north, with views over the Sea of Galilee, the Golan and the Yarmouk gorge. The restaurant terrace inside the site is a great lunch stop.
facts: ~5 JOD; Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Small museum in an Ottoman house
Clearest views in the morning or after rain

places.name: Pella (Tabaqat Fahl)
places.summary: Long-inhabited site in the Jordan Valley foothills, with a small Roman theatre, Byzantine churches and Bronze Age remains. Quiet and rarely visited.
facts: Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Rest house on the hill with a valley view
Hot in summer; visit in the morning

places.name: Irbid
places.summary: Jordan's second-largest urban area and a big student city, with the Dar as-Saraya museum in an Ottoman prison and a lively University Street. A practical base for Umm Qais.
facts: Dar as-Saraya museum in the old centre
University Street for cheap food and cafes
About 40 minutes from Umm Qais

places.name: Dibeen Forest Reserve
places.summary: Small RSCN reserve of Aleppo pine and oak near Jerash, popular with local families for picnics. Easy walking trails and a guesthouse.
facts: Quiet on weekdays, busy on Fridays
Short drive from Jerash
Pleasant picnic stop in spring

places.name: Anjara (Our Lady of the Mountain)
places.summary: Village near Ajloun with the Catholic shrine of Our Lady of the Mountain, where Jesus, Mary and the disciples are said to have rested in a cave. A pilgrimage stop on the way to Ajloun.
facts: Free; modest dress
Five minutes from Ajloun
Small church with a modern shrine

places.name: Mar Elias (Tell Mar Elias)
places.summary: Hilltop ruins of a large Byzantine church traditionally linked to the prophet Elijah, with mosaic floors and views over the Ajloun hills. A good stop on village walking routes.
facts: Free or small fee
Combine with Ajloun Castle and the forest reserve
Rough access road on the last stretch

places.name: King Talal Dam
places.summary: Jordan's largest reservoir, on the Zarqa River between Jerash and the Jordan Valley. A scenic pause on the back road between Jerash and the valley.
facts: Viewpoints along the road
No swimming
Quick stop of 15–20 minutes

places.name: Azraq
places.summary: Oasis town in the eastern desert at a crossroads of truck routes, with a Druze and a Chechen quarter. The base for Qasr al-Azraq, the wetland reserve and the desert castles loop.
facts: RSCN Azraq Lodge is the usual place to stay
Fuel up here before heading further east
About 1h20 from Amman on Highway 40

places.name: Qasr al-Azraq
places.summary: Black-basalt fortress used by Romans, Ayyubids and Ottomans, and T. E. Lawrence's winter headquarters in 1917–18. Note the huge single-slab stone door.
facts: Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Allow 45 minutes
A local guardian often shows you round

places.name: Qusayr 'Amra
places.summary: Small 8th-century Umayyad bathhouse and hunting lodge, a UNESCO site for its frescoes of hunting, bathing, musicians and the zodiac. The finest of the desert castles.
facts: ~2 JOD; Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Small visitor centre with explanations
On Highway 40 between Amman and Azraq

places.name: Qasr Kharana
places.summary: Fortress-looking Umayyad building of the early 8th century standing alone on the desert plain. Its two floors of rooms around a courtyard are probably a caravanserai or meeting hall rather than a fort.
facts: Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Allow 30–45 minutes
Right beside Highway 40

places.name: Azraq Wetland Reserve
places.summary: Restored remnant of a once-huge desert oasis, with a boardwalk through pools and reeds. Good for migrating birds and the endemic Azraq killifish.
facts: Small RSCN entry fee
Best for birds in spring and autumn migration
Short boardwalk loop of about 1.5 km

places.name: Shaumari Wildlife Reserve
places.summary: Breeding reserve where the Arabian oryx was reintroduced to Jordan, along with gazelles and onagers. Safari drives are run by the RSCN.
facts: Safaris must be booked through the RSCN
Early morning is best for animals
Small RSCN fee
Few kilometres south of Azraq

places.name: Umm el-Jimal
places.summary: Large ruined Byzantine and early Islamic town built entirely of black basalt, near the Syrian border, with houses, churches and water cisterns still standing several floors high. A UNESCO site since 2024.
facts: Free or small fee; visitor centre at the entrance
No shade; go early or late
About 1 hour from Jerash or Azraq

places.name: Qasr al-Hallabat
places.summary: Roman fort turned Umayyad palace, with remains of mosaics and a mosque, and the Hammam as-Sarah bathhouse a few kilometres away. The northern start of the desert castles loop.
facts: Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Combine with Hammam as-Sarah
Allow about 1 hour
Off the road between Zarqa and Azraq

places.name: Qasr Mshatta
places.summary: Unfinished 8th-century Umayyad palace just north of Queen Alia Airport. Its famous carved facade is in Berlin's Pergamon Museum, but the brick vaults and remaining stonework are worth a stop before a flight.
facts: Next to the airport; take your passport for the checkpoint
Allow 30–45 minutes
Free or small fee

places.name: Qasr Burqu'
places.summary: Remote Umayyad-era fort on the shore of a seasonal lake in the black basalt desert near the Iraqi border. Pure expedition territory for those wanting real emptiness.
facts: Needs a 4x4 and preferably a local guide
No services; carry water and fuel
Plan a full day from Azraq
places.caution: Very remote desert tracks close to the border: travel only with a guide and a fully equipped vehicle.

places.name: Qasr Tuba
places.summary: The remotest of the Umayyad desert castles, a huge unfinished brick and stone enclosure in the southern desert. Rarely visited and atmospheric.
facts: Reached only by long desert track; 4x4 and guide needed
No facilities; carry water and fuel
Plan a full day
places.caution: Remote off-road route with no phone signal or services.

places.name: Dead Sea (Sweimeh hotel strip)
places.summary: Strip of resort hotels on the north-east shore of the Dead Sea, about 430 m below sea level. Floating in the dense salty water is a classic experience, and the hotels give beach access, freshwater showers and mud.
facts: Hotel day passes are the easiest way to swim
Bring water shoes; the shore is rocky and salty
Under an hour from Amman and Madaba
places.season: Hot from May to September (often 40 °C); winter is mild and pleasant.
places.caution: Don't splash or put your head under: the water hurts eyes badly and is dangerous if swallowed; float on your back, stay 10–20 minutes, and shower afterwards.

places.name: Amman Beach (public Dead Sea beach)
places.summary: Public beach complex south of the resorts with showers, pools and shade, the cheapest organised way to float in the Dead Sea. Busy with local families on Fridays.
facts: Entry ~20 JOD
Bring your own towel
Quieter on weekdays
places.caution: Same Dead Sea rules: keep your head out of the water and rinse off afterwards.

places.name: Baptism Site (Al-Maghtas / Bethany beyond the Jordan)
places.summary: UNESCO site on the Jordan River where John is believed to have baptised Jesus, with excavated Byzantine churches and pools. Visits are by shuttle and guided walk to the river's edge.
facts: ~12 JOD; Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Guided tours by shuttle from the visitor centre
Allow 2 hours; very hot in summer, go early

places.name: Mount Nebo
places.summary: Hilltop where Moses is said to have seen the Promised Land, with a Franciscan memorial church full of Byzantine mosaics. On clear days you see the Dead Sea, Jericho and even Jerusalem.
facts: Entry ~3 JOD
Clearest views in the morning or after winter rain
15 minutes from Madaba

places.name: Madaba
places.summary: Relaxed, partly Christian town known for its Byzantine and Umayyad mosaics, including the famous mosaic map of the Holy Land. A calm alternative to Amman as a base, 30 minutes from the airport.
facts: Many family guesthouses and good restaurants
Easy base for Mount Nebo, the Dead Sea and the King's Highway
Visit the mosaic workshops

places.name: St George's Church & the Madaba Map
places.summary: Greek Orthodox church whose floor holds the 6th-century Madaba Map, the oldest surviving map of the Holy Land, with Jerusalem shown in detail. Short but essential.
facts: ~1 JOD
Closed to visits during Sunday morning services
Modest dress

places.name: Madaba Archaeological Park
places.summary: Group of excavated churches and a Roman street with some of the finest mosaics in Madaba, including the Church of the Virgin and the Hippolytus Hall. Combined ticket also covers the Church of the Apostles.
facts: ~3 JOD; Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Allow 45 minutes
In the centre of Madaba, a short walk from St George's

places.name: Wadi Mujib Siq Trail
places.summary: Wading and scrambling up a narrow sandstone gorge to a waterfall, from the Mujib Adventure Centre on the Dead Sea road. One of Jordan's most fun half-days in summer.
facts: Siq Trail ~21 JOD; guided trails cost more and should be booked with the RSCN
Open roughly April–October only
You will get wet up to the waist or chest; wear water shoes, bring a dry bag
Life jackets are provided
places.season: The Siq Trail is closed November–March because of flash-flood risk.
places.caution: Flash floods can hit after rain upstream; the trail closes when there is any risk, follow the rangers.

places.name: Ma'in Hot Springs (Hammamat Ma'in)
places.summary: Hot waterfalls tumbling down a desert gorge at around 60 °C, on the steep road between Madaba and the Dead Sea. Bathing is in the resort's pools and below the falls.
facts: Entry by resort day pass
Steep, winding road; drive carefully
Allow 2–3 hours
Busy with local families on Fridays
places.caution: The water near the source is scalding; bathe only where allowed.

places.name: Machaerus (Mukawir)
places.summary: Herod the Great's hilltop fortress where John the Baptist was imprisoned and beheaded, according to Josephus. A short steep walk leads to the summit with a sweeping view over the Dead Sea.
facts: Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
15-minute climb from the car park
Beautiful at sunset

places.name: Umm ar-Rasas
places.summary: UNESCO site of a Roman camp and Byzantine town with the superb mosaic floor of the Church of St Stephen, showing the cities of the region. A tall stylite tower stands nearby.
facts: Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Mosaic is under a protective roof
About 40 minutes south-east of Madaba

places.name: Dead Sea Panorama Complex
places.summary: Clifftop viewpoint and small museum above the Dead Sea on the road to Ma'in, explaining the sea's geology and shrinking level. Short trails and a restaurant with a superb view.
facts: Small entry fee
Best at sunset
Short walk along the cliff edge
Restaurant with Dead Sea views

places.name: Lot's Cave & Museum at the Lowest Point on Earth
places.summary: Cave and Byzantine monastery on a hillside above Ghor as-Safi, linked to Lot fleeing Sodom. The museum below holds finds from the area and explains the southern Dead Sea.
facts: Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD) (museum)
Steep stairs to the cave
Hot most of the year; go early

places.name: Hammam as-Sarah
places.summary: Restored Umayyad bathhouse a few kilometres from Qasr al-Hallabat, with a domed hot room and the remains of its water system. A quick stop on the northern desert-castles loop.
facts: Small open site, usually free
Combine with Qasr al-Hallabat
Little shade; go in the morning

places.name: Kerak (Al-Karak)
places.summary: Hilltop town on the King's Highway, wrapped around one of the great Crusader castles. A useful overnight stop on the slow road between Madaba and Petra.
facts: Simple hotels near the castle
Kerak is the halfway point Madaba–Dana
About 1h45 from Amman via the Desert Highway

places.name: Kerak Castle
places.summary: Huge 12th-century Crusader castle later rebuilt by the Mamluks, with long vaulted halls, passages and towers to explore. Bring a torch for the dark galleries.
facts: ~2 JOD; Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Small archaeological museum inside
Allow 1.5 hours; uneven floors and dark passages

places.name: Wadi Mujib Canyon (King's Highway)
places.summary: Where the King's Highway drops about 1 km into the great Mujib gorge and climbs out again in hairpins, passing the dam. Stop at the rim viewpoints for the 'Grand Canyon of Jordan'.
facts: Viewpoints at the north and south rims
Slow road with sharp bends
Allow 30 minutes for photos
Fuel up in Madaba or Kerak

places.name: Wadi Bin Hammad
places.summary: Palm-lined canyon with warm springs and hanging gardens of ferns, walked in the stream bed below Kerak's hills. Less known and less wet than Mujib.
facts: Walk in the stream; wear shoes that can get wet
Rough final road; a local guide helps
Allow 3–4 hours
places.caution: Do not enter if rain is forecast: flash-flood risk.

places.name: Tafilah
places.summary: Provincial town on the King's Highway with a small Crusader-era castle, between Kerak and Dana. Mostly a fuel and food stop.
facts: Supplies before Dana
Small castle in the town centre
Afra hot springs nearby

places.name: Wadi Hasa
places.summary: Long canyon from the plateau down towards the Dead Sea, with hot springs and pools; the King's Highway crosses its upper part with big views. The full descent is an all-day wade.
facts: Full canyon trek needs a guide and a vehicle pick-up
Best April–October
Viewpoints where the King's Highway crosses
places.caution: Serious flash-flood risk after rain; never descend when storms are possible.

places.name: Afra Hot Springs
places.summary: Hot springs in a narrow, steep-walled valley north of Tafilah, with simple pools fed by water at around 45 °C. Popular with locals on weekends.
facts: Small entry fee
Busy on Fridays; quieter on weekdays
Steep, narrow access road
Separate bathing times may apply for families

places.name: Dana
places.summary: Restored 15th-century stone village perched on the rim of the Dana valley, the gateway to the Dana Biosphere Reserve. Views down to Wadi Araba and great sunsets.
facts: Simple guesthouses and the RSCN Dana Guesthouse
Start of the Dana–Feynan trail
Cold at night in winter

places.name: Dana Biosphere Reserve
places.summary: Jordan's largest nature reserve, dropping from 1,500 m to below sea level through four climate zones, with ibex, rare plants and Nabataean copper mines. Rummana campsite and short trails sit near the top.
facts: Small RSCN entry fee; guided trails booked with the RSCN
Short trails from Rummana campsite
Spring and autumn are best for hiking
places.season: Spring and autumn are ideal; the lowlands are very hot in summer.

places.name: Wadi Dana Trail (Dana to Feynan)
places.summary: Classic one-way walk of about 14 km down the Dana valley from Dana village to Feynan Ecolodge, through changing landscapes. Mostly downhill and unguided-friendly, ending in candlelit Feynan.
facts: About 5–6 hours, 1,200 m of descent
Arrange luggage transfer and a ride back
Start early; carry plenty of water
places.caution: Very hot in the lower valley from May to September; walk only in the cool season.

places.name: Feynan
places.summary: Remote area of Wadi Feynan at the bottom of the Dana reserve, best known for its solar-powered, candlelit ecolodge run with local Bedouin. Stay for stargazing, hikes and Bedouin activities.
facts: Last part of the access is a 4x4 track; transfers from Qurayqira
Book the ecolodge well in advance
Mid-day heat is extreme in summer

places.name: Wadi Ghuweir
places.summary: Spectacular water-filled canyon walked from the plateau down to Feynan, through narrow siqs, palms and pools. One of Jordan's finest day hikes.
facts: Guide strongly recommended; bookable at Feynan
About 6 hours; you will wade
Season roughly March–October
places.caution: Flash floods are a real danger: never enter if rain is forecast anywhere upstream.

places.name: Shobak Castle (Montreal)
places.summary: Crusader castle of 1115 on a lonely conical hill, the first built by King Baldwin I in the region. Atmospheric ruins with a long secret staircase down to a well.
facts: Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Allow 1 hour; bring a torch for the tunnel
30 minutes north of Wadi Musa

places.name: Wadi Musa
places.summary: Town next to the entrance of Petra with most of the hotels, restaurants and Turkish baths. You will need at least one or two nights here to see Petra properly.
facts: Stay at least two nights to see Petra unhurried
Hotels near the visitor centre save walking
Cold at night in winter (it can snow)

places.name: Petra
places.summary: The Nabataean rock-cut city, with tombs, temples and theatres carved into rose-red sandstone and reached through the narrow Siq. A UNESCO site and one of the New Seven Wonders, it deserves at least one full day.
facts: 1 day ~50 JOD, 2 days ~55, 3 days ~60; ~90 JOD if you don't stay overnight in Jordan — Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Expect 15–20 km of walking on a full day
Enter at opening for the Siq and Treasury without crowds
Bring water, sun protection and good shoes
places.season: Best March–May and October–November; summer afternoons are very hot, winter can be cold with rare flash floods.
places.caution: Long walks with steep stairs and strong sun: carry water and turn back early rather than late.

places.name: The Siq
places.summary: The 1.2 km winding gorge, in places only a few metres wide, that forms Petra's main entrance. It opens dramatically onto the Treasury.
facts: Included in the Petra ticket
About 2 km walk from the gate to the Treasury
Horse-carts run for those who can't walk

places.name: The Treasury (Al-Khazneh)
places.summary: Petra's famous 40 m facade, carved as a royal tomb in the 1st century AD, seen first at the end of the Siq. Morning sun lights it best.
facts: Included in the Petra ticket
Before 08:00 it is almost empty
Best light from mid-morning

places.name: Royal Tombs
places.summary: Row of grand tomb facades on the al-Khubtha cliff, including the Urn, Silk and Corinthian tombs, with swirling coloured sandstone inside. Climb the stairs for views over the city centre.
facts: Included in the Petra ticket
Late afternoon light is best on these west-facing facades
Allow about 1 hour

places.name: Qasr al-Bint & the Colonnaded Street
places.summary: The heart of Nabataean Petra: a paved Roman colonnaded street leading past the Great Temple to Qasr al-Bint, the city's main temple. Restaurants and rest stops are nearby.
facts: Included in the Petra ticket
Start of the climb to the Monastery
Allow about 1 hour

places.name: The Monastery (Ad Deir)
places.summary: Petra's largest facade, reached by about 800 rock-cut steps from the city centre. The climb takes around 45 minutes; viewpoints beyond look over Wadi Araba.
facts: Included in the Petra ticket
Climb in the afternoon when the stairs are in shade
Donkeys are offered; please avoid overloaded or mistreated animals
places.caution: Steep steps and heat: carry water and allow 3 hours for the round trip from the city centre.

places.name: High Place of Sacrifice
places.summary: Steep stairway climb to a Nabataean altar platform with views over Petra, returning via Wadi Farasa past the Lion Fountain and Garden Tomb. A quieter loop than the main valley.
facts: About 2–3 hours for the loop
Start near the Theatre
Included in the Petra ticket

places.name: Al-Khubtha Trail (Treasury viewpoint)
places.summary: Stairway trail up the al-Khubtha ridge from the Royal Tombs to a viewpoint looking straight down onto the Treasury. The classic aerial photo of Petra.
facts: About 2 hours return
A Bedouin tea stall sits at the viewpoint (small fee is often asked)
Best in morning light for the Treasury view

places.name: Little Petra to the Monastery (back trail)
places.summary: Walk into Petra from the north via Little Petra and the Umm Sayhoun area, arriving at the Monastery from behind before descending to the centre. Quieter than the Siq approach.
facts: About 3–4 hours; a guide is strongly recommended
Valid Petra ticket required
Arrange transport to the trailhead

places.name: Petra by Night
places.summary: Walk through the Siq lit by about 1,500 candles to the Treasury for Bedouin music and tea. Atmospheric if a little crowded.
facts: ~17 JOD, separate from the day ticket
Usually Monday, Wednesday and Thursday at 20:30
Lasts about 2 hours

places.name: Petra Museum
places.summary: Modern museum at the visitor centre with finds from Petra and an introduction to the Nabataeans. Good for an hour before or after the site.
facts: Free
At the Petra Visitor Centre
Air-conditioned; good in the heat of the day

places.name: Little Petra (Siq al-Barid)
places.summary: Small Nabataean suburb in a narrow canyon, with carved houses, cisterns and a rare painted ceiling. Free, uncrowded and a good taste of Petra on arrival day.
facts: Free
15 minutes' drive north of Wadi Musa
Combine with Beidha

places.name: Beidha Neolithic Village
places.summary: Excavated Neolithic village around 9,000 years old, with reconstructed round houses, a short walk from Little Petra. Among the oldest villages in the Middle East.
facts: Free
Short walk from the Little Petra car park
Allow 30 minutes

places.name: Jabal Haroun (Aaron's Tomb)
places.summary: Long hike to the highest peak around Petra, topped by a white shrine traditionally the tomb of Aaron, brother of Moses. Wild views over Petra and Wadi Araba.
facts: About 6 hours return from the city centre
Guide recommended
Valid Petra ticket required
places.caution: Exposed and very hot in summer; start early with plenty of water.

places.name: Wadi Rum village
places.summary: Small Bedouin village at the foot of Jebel Rum, the starting point for jeep tours, camel treks and nights in desert camps. Most visitors sleep in camps further into the protected area.
facts: Book a camp and tour in advance; most include pick-up from the village
Nights are cold from November to March
ATM and shops are basic; bring cash
places.season: Spring and autumn are ideal; summer days are scorching, winter nights near freezing.

places.name: Wadi Rum Protected Area (jeep tour)
places.summary: UNESCO desert of red sand and towering sandstone mountains, explored by 4x4 with Bedouin guides from the visitor centre. A half-day or full-day jeep tour links the main canyons, dunes and rock bridges.
facts: Entry ~5 JOD; Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Tours start at the visitor centre or in Rum village
Full day with sunset is best; stay overnight for the stars

places.name: Seven Pillars of Wisdom
places.summary: Fluted rock face near the visitor centre named after T. E. Lawrence's book. A quick photo stop on the way in.
facts: Visible from the visitor centre
Free with Wadi Rum entry
A few minutes' stop

places.name: Lawrence's Spring
places.summary: Small spring up a rocky slope where Lawrence is said to have washed during the Arab Revolt, with Nabataean inscriptions and a fine view over the valley. A standard first jeep-tour stop.
facts: Short scramble up from the jeep track
Standard stop on jeep tours
Allow 30–45 minutes

places.name: Khazali Canyon
places.summary: Narrow cleft in Jebel Khazali with Thamudic and Nabataean petroglyphs of people, camels and footprints. Cool and shady even at midday.
facts: Standard stop on jeep tours
Only the first part is walkable without climbing
Allow 20–30 minutes

places.name: Red Sand Dunes
places.summary: Tall dune of deep red sand banked against a mountain, perfect for climbing and running down. Best in late afternoon light.
facts: Go barefoot in the cool season; sand burns in summer
Standard stop on jeep tours
Late afternoon light is best

places.name: Umm Fruth Rock Bridge
places.summary: Small natural arch about 15 m high that you can scramble onto for photos. One of the most visited spots on jeep tours.
facts: Easy scramble, care on the way down
Standard stop on jeep tours
Queues for photos at midday

places.name: Burdah Rock Bridge
places.summary: High natural arch on Jebel Burdah reached by a scrambling ascent of about 1.5 hours. The view from the bridge over the desert is spectacular.
facts: Guide required; some exposed scrambling
About 3 hours return
Start early to avoid the heat
places.caution: Exposed scrambling with drops: not for those uneasy with heights.

places.name: Jebel Umm ad-Dami
places.summary: Jordan's highest mountain at about 1,850 m, in the far south of Wadi Rum near the Saudi border. A steep ascent leads to views towards the Red Sea on clear days.
facts: Needs a long jeep transfer and a guide
About 3 hours return from the base
Start early; the summit is exposed

places.name: Hot-air balloon over Wadi Rum
places.summary: Sunrise balloon flights over the mountains and sands of Wadi Rum, run from near the visitor centre. Expensive but unforgettable.
facts: Book in advance; weather dependent
Very early pick-up
Flights last about 1 hour

places.name: Disi
places.summary: Bedouin village on the north-eastern edge of the Wadi Rum desert, surrounded by camps and a quieter alternative to Rum village. Several camps here offer jeep and camel trips.
facts: Many camps; arrange pick-up in advance
Quieter than Rum village
About 25 minutes from Rum village

places.name: Humayma
places.summary: Remote ruins of a Nabataean, Roman and early Abbasid settlement off the Desert Highway, where the Abbasid family plotted their rise to power. Extensive water channels and cisterns.
facts: Unpaved access track
No facilities
Allow about 1 hour

places.name: Aqaba
places.summary: Jordan's only seaport and a duty-free beach town on the Red Sea, with a laid-back downtown, fish restaurants and coral reefs a few kilometres south. A good rest stop after Petra and Wadi Rum.
facts: Hotels from simple downtown to resorts south at Tala Bay
Aqaba is a special economic zone with low-tax shopping
Ferries to Egypt (Nuweiba/Taba) leave from the port south of town
places.season: Warm all year; swimming is pleasant even in winter, summer is very hot.

places.name: Aqaba Fort
places.summary: Mamluk fort of the 16th century famous for the 1917 capture by the Arab Revolt and Lawrence. Next to the giant Aqaba flagpole and the waterfront.
facts: Covered by the Jordan Pass (~70–80 JOD)
Combine with a walk along the corniche
Allow 30–45 minutes

places.name: Ayla (early Islamic Aqaba)
places.summary: Excavated walls, gates and streets of the 7th-century Islamic town of Ayla right on the seafront. Free and easy to see while walking the corniche.
facts: Free; open site
Interpretive signs on site
Allow 30 minutes

places.name: Aqaba Church
places.summary: Foundations of a late-3rd-century building considered one of the oldest purpose-built churches in the world. Brief stop near Ayla.
facts: Free; viewed through the fence
Next to Ayla on the seafront
Quick 15–20 minute stop

places.name: Aqaba downtown souk
places.summary: Compact downtown market of spice, sweet and souvenir shops, with simple fish and falafel restaurants. Best after dark when it cools down.
facts: Lively in the evening
Try sayadieh (spiced fish and rice)
Cheap sweets and spices

places.name: Glass-bottom boat trip
places.summary: Short boat trips from the town beach over the reefs south of Aqaba, with views of the coral and fish without getting wet. Some include snorkelling stops.
facts: Agree price and duration before boarding
Morning seas are calmest
Boats leave from the downtown beach

places.name: Aqaba Marine Park
places.summary: Protected stretch of coast south of the port with fringing coral reefs right off the beach, including the Japanese Garden. Easy snorkelling and diving with dive centres along the shore.
facts: Dive centres rent snorkel gear and run trips
Water shoes protect against urchins
Don't stand on or touch the coral

places.name: Cedar Pride wreck
places.summary: Lebanese cargo ship scuttled in 1985 as an artificial reef, now covered in soft corals at 7–27 m depth. Aqaba's most famous dive, also visible in part to snorkellers.
facts: Book with a dive centre
Shore dive from the beach
Snorkellers can see the upper parts

places.name: South Beach
places.summary: The beaches south of the port with clearer water and reefs, a mix of public stretches and paid beach clubs. Better for swimming than the town beach.
facts: Beach clubs charge a day fee
Modest swimwear is respected on public beaches
Bring water shoes for the reefs

places.name: Tala Bay
places.summary: Resort and marina development near the Saudi border with hotels, a sandy beach and dive centres. Convenient for diving trips.
facts: Resort hotels; taxis to downtown Aqaba ~20 minutes
Sandy beach and dive centres
Close to the Saudi border; the coast road ends here

places.name: Japanese Garden reef
places.summary: Shallow coral garden in the Aqaba Marine Park, named for its neat clusters of hard and soft corals. One of the easiest and prettiest snorkel and dive sites off the shore.
facts: Reached by boat or a swim from the shore
Dive centres nearby run trips
Calmest in the morning

places.name: Aqaba Flagpole & Arab Revolt Plaza
places.summary: Giant flagpole flying the flag of the Great Arab Revolt beside Aqaba Fort, visible from Egypt, Israel and Saudi Arabia. The plaza is a popular evening promenade.
facts: Free
Next to Aqaba Fort
Pleasant at sunset

places.name: Queen Alia Airport, Amman (AMM)
places.summary: Jordan's main airport, 35 km south of Amman on the Desert Highway: about 40 min to the city, and on the way to the Dead Sea and the south.
facts: Visa on arrival, or free with the Jordan Pass (3+ nights)
Car rental desks in arrivals; the Airport Express bus runs to Amman
Allow 3 h before international flights: security is thorough

places.name: King Hussein Airport, Aqaba (AQJ)
places.summary: Aqaba's airport, 10 km north of town: Royal Jordanian flights to Amman and seasonal charters from Europe. Handy for Wadi Rum and Petra.
facts: About 1 h flight to Amman
Aqaba is a special economic zone: duty-free shopping

bookings.note: Amman (AMM); some seasonal flights go straight to Aqaba (AQJ).
Wanderer 70 / Explorer 75 / Expert 80 JOD: 1, 2 or 3 days in Petra. Buy before you arrive.
Per week, small car. Or a driver for the King's Highway day.

bookings.item: Wadi Rum camp and jeep tour
bookings.note: Per person: a night in a camp with dinner, and a half-day jeep tour.
Easier than the free public beaches: showers, pools and shade.

links.name: Jordan Pass
links.note: Buy before you arrive: entry to Petra and ~40 sites, and the visa fee waived if you stay 3+ nights.

links.name: Visit Petra
links.note: Petra opening hours, tickets and Petra by Night dates.

links.name: Visit Jordan (tourism board)
links.note: Official tourism site: regions, events and practical information.

links.name: RSCN nature reserves
links.note: Dana, Wadi Mujib, Ajloun and Azraq reserves: trails, guides and lodges. Some trails need booking.

links.name: Jordan Meteorological Department
links.note: Forecasts and warnings: flash floods, dust storms and the rare winter snow.

links.name: JETT buses
links.note: Tourist buses Amman ↔ Petra ↔ Aqaba if you don't drive.

checklist: Passport valid 6+ months. Visa on arrival, or buy the Jordan Pass online before you fly: it waives the visa fee if you stay at least 3 nights.
Driving licence (an International Driving Permit is recommended); credit card for the rental deposit.
Dress modestly away from the beach resorts: shoulders and knees covered; a headscarf for women in mosques.
Friday is the weekend: some sites, shops and offices open late or close early. Ramadan changes opening hours and restaurant times.
Petra: walking shoes, sun hat, 2–3 l of water a day; start at opening time to beat the heat and the groups.
Wadi Mujib Siq Trail opens only from about April to October, and closes on days with flood risk.
Dead Sea: don't shave the day before, keep the water out of your eyes, and float, don't swim face down.
Night driving: unlit roads, speed bumps and animals. Plan long drives in daylight.
Book Wadi Rum camps and jeep tours ahead in spring and autumn.
Travel insurance that covers hiking and desert activities.
